newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP at loggerheads with Fischler over ACP bananas.
newsitem.headline: EP at loggerheads with Fischler over ACP bananas.

text.p: The European Parliament refused on Friday to approve a European Commission proposal to cut the quantity of bananas which former European colonies are allowed to export to the EU market.
Euro-MPs voted to refer the proposal -- COM(96)82 -- back to the agriculture committee after Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said he could not accept their amendments to the text.
The Commission proposed in March increasing the overall tariff quota from 2.2 million tonnes to 2.553 million tonnes, to account for the accession of Austria, Finland and Sweden.
At the same time, it proposed raising from 66.5 to 70.5 percent the share of the EU market allotted to suppliers of Latin American bananas -- mainly U.S.-based multinationals.

The extra percentage would be found by cutting from 30 percent to 26 percent the share of the banana tariff quota allotted to traditional suppliers from Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific (ACP states).

Parliament on Friday approved amendments to the proposal which would reinstate the ACP states' 30 percent share of the market and provide for an overall tariff quota increase of only 100,000 tonnes (to 2.3 million tonnes).
Fischler told Parliament a 100,000-tonne increase would not be enough to satisfy the extra demand for bananas caused by Austria, Finland and Sweden joining the EU.

But a report on the banana regime by Italian Union for Europe Euro-MP Giacomo Santini says the EU market has been saturated since June 1995, resulting in price slumps which have severely affected the ACP producers, who are less competitive than their "dollar" banana rivals.

Fischler also told parliament that increasing the ACPs' share of the enlarged quota went against the "traditional trade pattern" because only Latin American dollar bananas were marketed in the three new EU member states.
Santini said in his report that this argument was "an absurd assertion which runs counter to a single market and a common market organisation".

In addition, the Commission's proposal undermined the EU's commitment, enshrined in a protocol on bananas, to ensure that conditions imposed on ACP states would never be worse than those of the past, the report said.
"The 30 percent tariff quota volume amounts to the minimum compensation required in order to guarantee their survival and offer any sort of prospects for the future," it stressed.
